last_action.summary: Implemented B1-M2-P1. Inspection (verified live 2026-09-07) settled the schema: one authoritative series (WDFW + Muckleshoot at the Ballard Locks ladder), so the constraint is (date, species) with source as provenance -- strengthened by finding that the two retrieval routes OVERLAP on current-season sockeye, so keying on source would double-count one observation. Found an undocumented JSON feed behind the page's chart (pssp-count.wdfw-fish.us) carrying 17 seasons of daily sockeye in one download. Four findings that change downstream plans: Chinook/coho history is absent from both LIVE sources but IS available in archived snapshots of the WDFW page -- CORRECTED after human challenge; the first pass wrongly concluded no multi-year history existed at all. Verified by parsing 7 archived post-season snapshots: sockeye 17 seasons (2010-2026, one JSON download), chinook 7 (2020-2026), coho 8 (2019-2026), one programmatic fetch per year. Chinook/coho still miss Q-006's 10-year floor, but by a near-miss rather than a wall. Reasoning error worth remembering: I invoked the history-depth soft cap, which exists to avoid per-year-per-species MANUAL extraction, without checking whether that was the actual cost -- it was not. Unexplored lead left open for next session: the legacy pre-2019 WDFW counts section (wdfw.wa.gov/fishing/counts/sockeye/, archived back to 2010, containing archives.html plus chinook and coho chart JPEGs) could push past the floor if it holds tables rather than only images. No schema or code change resulted; the constraint and vocabulary are unaffected and the P1 commits stand; the JSON's count_Nyear keys are relative to the current year, not calendar (verified by matching the 2017/2013 spikes against the independent annual table); blank cells are pre-rendered for the whole season and must not be read as zero; multi-day range rows exist and cannot be stored. Recent-window question dissolved -- the source serves the full season in one document and warns counts are revised, so re-parse the whole season every run. Built apps/salmon with both models, three DB-level constraints verified in the DDL (unique (date,species), closed species vocabulary, correction-note-required), admin for both, 24 tests passing, makemigrations --check clean, migrate verified on a genuinely fresh DB. Corrected two prior assumptions: steelhead is not published at this ladder (no vocabulary member created; the SALMON_SPECIES subset structure retained and the affected DECISIONS entry annotated to avoid a standing contradiction), and the source gives a per-row Running Total, enabling a per-date parser checksum rather than a season-end one. Commit a709172 on feat/salmon-ballard-locks (not pushed). Full pytest suite deliberately NOT run -- deferred to milestone end per human direction mid-phase; caveat recorded in thread since this phase did touch settings.py and urls.py, both covered by a passing manage.py check. STATUS.md skipped (status_updates=pm_only). P1 is not the last phase and code_review=every_milestone, so routing to PM.StatusUpdate. SESSION PAUSED at human request mid-turn on 2026-09-07; resuming next session. Correction recorded in plans/thread.md and docs/data-sources.md. Nothing pushed in either repo.

context.goal: A small mobile-first website that answers whether salmon are currently visible at Ballard Locks and forecasts total salmon expected over the next 7 days, combining crowd YES/NO reports with locally stored official/historical fish-count data.
notes: STATE is the routing source of truth.
STATUS must be updated every action.

Thread is active working memory; prune when there is genuinely prunable/promotable content, not merely because it is long (prunability gate — see plans/README.md 'Thread management' and D-026). Cannot prune before most content before Code Review and Human Approval.
